newsitem.title: USA: Amphenol to be bought by KKR affiliate.
newsitem.headline: Amphenol to be bought by KKR affiliate.

text.p: Amphenol Corp., a maker of electronics and industrial connectors and cable, said Thursday it has agreed to be acquired by Kohlberg Kravis Roberts & Co., in a deal worth $1.5 billion including refinanced debt.
Under the agreement, NXS Acquisition Corp., a KKR affiliate, will offer $26 in cash for a majority of Amphenol's stock, giving NXS control of more than 75 percent of the company.
Amphenol stockholders can choose to keep up to 4.4 million or 10 percent of the company's 44.7 million shares outstanding, valued at $1.16 billion.
Amphenol rose $2.625 to $25.75 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Amphenol Chairman Lawrence DeGeorge, his family and an associated trust with a total 30 percent of Amphenol's outstanding shares have agreed to vote in favour of the deal, Amphenol said.
KKR, through affiliates, will invest up to $374 million in the deal, while the rest of the $1.5 billion will come from bank or subordinated debt, a KKR spokeswoman said.
Amphenol will continue to be run by current management at its Wallingford, Conn., headquarters.

Amphenol manufactures connectors, cable and interconnect systems for electronics, cable television, telecommunications, aerospace, transportation and industrial applications. The products are made in North America, Europe and the Far East.
